title: Value Added Tax Law, 5736-1975
source_id: ס״ח תשל״ו, 52; Knesset legislation database lawitemid 2001068; Wikisource page חוק מס ערך מוסף
verified_how: Fetched the Wikisource page. Heading prints חוק מס ערך מוסף, תשל״ו–1975; metadata gives the Sefer HaChukim citation at page 52 of the תשל״ו volume and Knesset lawitemid 2001068; most recent amendment noted תשפ״ו, 405 (2026). On import: s 2 imposes VAT on a transaction in Israel and on the import of goods (יבוא טובין) at the rate set by the Minister of Finance; s 11(א) values imported goods by reference to the customs valuation provisions of the Customs Ordinance (ss 129 to 134א), plus the customs duty and any other tax or levy applying on the import; s 26(א) fixes the time the tax on import becomes chargeable.
notes: Included because it bears directly on import duties, but it is NOT the customs charging instrument: VAT on import is a separate tax, imposed by s 2 of this Law, calculated on a base that includes the customs duty (s 11(א)) and that borrows the Customs Ordinance valuation rules (ss 129-134א). At the border a single import therefore attracts up to three charges under three different instruments: customs duty (1937 Ordinance at the 2017 tariff order rates), purchase tax (Purchase Tax (Goods and Services) Law, 5712-1952, with rates in the same 2017 order), and VAT (this Law). The VAT rate itself is set by order of the Minister of Finance under s 2, not in the Law, so the standard rate cannot be read off the statute.
